title: Install stitching & interop weekly - Aug 2027
content:
Weekly sync notes (Aug 10 - Aug 12, 2027)

Attendees: Sara Liu (owner), Marco Reyes, Priya Nair, Ethan Cole, Jasmine Park, support reps from Project Orchid (customer), ops lead from Nimbus Finch (customer).

Purpose: Triage current VPC/on-prem install interop issues (the "stitching" layer between customer network topologies, our install automation, and runtime kernel/driver constraints). Capture immediate blockers, decisions, and owners for the coming week.

Agenda:
- Quick status per active install
- Deep dive: MTU/BGP oddness observed in two installs
- Authentication flap after KMS rotation
- Runbook/installer change proposals and rollout plan
- Action items and owners

Summary / key takeaways:
1) Two installs (Orchid - managed colo, and Nimbus Finch - hybrid VPC with direct-connect) both hit the same symptom class: intermittent inter-node gRPC failures under 1.5s token bursts. Root cause appears to be packet fragmentation caused by MTU mismatch + our prefix-preserving NAT rule that doubles header size for certain encapsulation modes.
2) On Orchid we confirmed the customer’s edge router is advertising 1500 MTU but the on-prem switch stack enforces 1400 on the ML cluster VLAN. When our init script sets up vxlan overlay, it didn't detect the lowered MTU and defaulted to 1450 for encap overhead assumptions -> fragmentation at ~1.2MB/s load.
3) Nimbus Finch reported a BGP flap that coincided with node reboots during an upgrade. The BGP session was timing out because the kube-proxy restart re-triggered iptables rules deletion briefly; we saw RSTs for the Redis KV proxy causing cache misses and upstream fallback to slower model variants.
4) One install saw credential failures immediately after a scheduled KMS key rotation (PD-3124). The private-control-plane microservice had cached an ARN token and did not pick up the rotated key due to a race in the refresh path. That token now fails with 403 until a restart or explicit refresh.

Per-install notes:
- Project Orchid (managed colo)
  - Status: degraded (intermittent RPC failures)
  - Investigation: Marco reproduced fragmentation locally with a constrained MTU test; confirmed overlay settings in our installer do not query underlying interface MTU before creating vxlan.
  - Immediate mitigation: adjust vxlan mtu to min(detected-encap, 1300) via emergency hotfix (installer v0.9.3-hotfix).
  - Impact: API latency spikes for short bursts; no data loss.
  - Open tickets: PD-3190 (Orchid-mtu-fix) assigned to Marco, due 2027-08-13.

- Nimbus Finch (hybrid VPC + DC)
  - Status: partial outage for model-serving path during upgrades
  - Investigation: sequence: upgrade job -> kubelet restart -> kube-proxy restart -> iptables flush window -> BGP keepalive missed -> BGP flap -> intermittent path blackholing.
  - Workaround: stagger control-plane restarts, add a 15s drain-and-wait before kube-proxy restart in our upgrade playbook.
  - Longer-term: make kube-proxy restart idempotent w.r.t BGP adjacency (PR linked). Jasmine to prototype change. Target: reduce upgrade window to <30s without triggering BGP flap.

- Generic on-prem installs (field)
  - Observed: some OS images (Debian-12 with older kernel 6.1 backport) have conntrack timeouts lower than defaults; causes short-lived TCP resets under high concurrent token streams.
  - Action: add a post-install sysctl step to normalize net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established to 432000. Priya to add to runbook template.

Telemetry & logs called out:
- Collected pcap from Orchid (s3://redwood-telemetry/orchid/2027-08-09-pcap) showed fragmentation flags set and reassembly occurring.
- Nimbus Finch BGP logs: abrupt TCP RSTs before keepalive window.
- Auth service rotation logs: PD-3124 shows successful rotation but missing refresh handshake for private-control-plane.

Decisions made:
- Emergency hotfix for vxlan MTU detection (v0.9.3-hotfix) will be rolled to affected installs first, then baked into mainline installer if no regressions.
- Add an optional installer flag --detect-interface-mtu to enable conservative encap sizing by default.
- Change upgrade playbook: control-plane component restarts must be serialized and include a 15s quiesce period before network-critical restarts.

Action items (owner - due):
- Marco Reyes - implement and test vxlan mtu detection + ship v0.9.3-hotfix (due 2027-08-13) [PD-3190].
- Priya Nair - add conntrack sysctl post-install step and update template docs; include verify checklist (due 2027-08-16).
- Jasmine Park - prototype kube-proxy/BGP adjacency hardening (PR + bench notes) (due 2027-08-18).
- Ethan Cole - implement token refresh path fix for private-control-plane (PD-3124 follow-up) with graceful backoff; add unit tests (due 2027-08-14).
- Sara Liu - coordinate hotfix rollout with Customer Success for Orchid & Nimbus Finch; prepare rollback plan and SLAs comms (due 2027-08-13).

Risks and open questions:
- Will conservative vxlan mtu sizing cause throughput regressions for customers with jumbo frames? Need to gate via installer flag and better detection.
- Is there a systematic way to detect kernel-level conntrack tiling on first boot across our supported images? Consider a lightweight bootstrap test.
- KMS rotation race: do we require a central refresh bus / webhook to notify control-plane instances to refresh post-rotation? Possible infra change that touches sensitive auth paths.

Runbook / process updates proposed:
- Add "Network MTU check" step to preflight with explicit fallback values and a note on jumbo frames.
- Add "quiesce window" guidance to upgrade playbooks for control-plane components to avoid transient BGP adjacencies.
- Add a standard post-install sysctl verification checklist.

Meeting notes (quick timeline):
- 08:10 - quick per-install status
- 08:25 - Marco presented MTU repro steps and demo pcap
- 08:40 - Jasmine and Priya discussed upgrade playbook adjustments
- 08:58 - Action owners assigned and deadlines agreed

Next check-in: Friday, Aug 13 2027, 08:00 PT (standup to verify hotfix rollout state).

Notes to self: document the exact repro harness for MTU fragmentation as a runnable script (so Field can re-run locally), and add a flag to telemetry agent to auto-capture MTU on first boot.

Attachments/reference: PD-3124, PD-3190, pcap link (internal), installer PR #487.
